findings.claim: Endpoint-coordinate effects are dominated by shape (pose-invariant) descriptors rather than global centroid translation: shape_yy shows the strongest integrated high-low contrast with all batches agreeing in sign, and shape_xx is similarly negative, whereas global_centroid_x and global_centroid_z have intervals spanning zero. This separates global pose from shape information.

global_centroid_y is the only centroid component with a q-significant integrated effect, but its positive_batch_fraction is low (0.21), so the mean is carried by a minority of batches; this is weaker and less reproducible than the shape effects and should not be prioritized as a coordinate rule on point estimate alone.

Continuous contrast features over the observed window are non-monotone: landmark_00_local_dy and landmark_00_local_dz show multiple sign changes with large opposing first/last rate z-values, and polynomial fits are not accepted (extrapolation_allowed false, observed_node_linear). A constant rule is therefore not supported by these curves; any time-conditioned use must stay within the observed support.

Several local landmark features (e.g. landmark_00_local_dx, landmark_00_local_cyy) have large opposing first and last rate z-values with multiple strong sign conflicts, indicating rate changes within the window rather than a stable direction; these are not reliable constant-direction coordinate rewards.

hypotheses.falsifier: shape_yy or shape_xx integrated contrast loses sign consistency across independent batches or its q-value rises above the multiplicity threshold
hypotheses.observable: integrated high-low contrast of shape_yy and shape_xx over the observed window
hypotheses.scope: observed endpoint world-coordinate features, learning window [0,0.5]
hypotheses.statement: A shape-oriented coordinate reward (targeting shape_yy and shape_xx reduction) will improve final predicted target affinity more than a global-centroid translation reward, because shape effects are the only endpoint contrasts with consistent batch sign agreement.

hypotheses.falsifier: a constant rule matches the observed-node interpolation within the reported relative node RMSE
hypotheses.observable: first vs last rate z of landmark_00_local_dy and landmark_00_local_dz
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule for local landmark rates is preferable to a constant rule, since local_dy/local_dz rates change sign within the observed window.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or current-study outcome data are supplied, so last-record/endpoint credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the immediate-selection vs descendant-survival comparison is unavailable.

Ancestral coverage and survivor-bias diagnostics (lineage_support, turnover_accounting, increment_effects, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, branch_adjusted) were not read within the turn budget; multiplicity-adjusted ranking and parent-child increment decomposition remain unverified.
Continuous contrast curves are coordinate rewards, not absolute affinity targets or trajectory velocity forces; no causal neural-module claim is supported.
Temperature and other fixed task parameters were not examined and are not proposed for edit.
